name: Pia Burke
life: “I still remember watching a custody handover go perfectly quietly.” On Saturday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Pia checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I thanked my ex. A good custody calendar is worth more to both of us than another argument over uniforms.
appearance: Pia has thick, tightly coiled hair, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Pia steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Pia never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Pia can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To recognize the ex's work on the custody calendar.
family: Jody Breen is Pia’s parent’s cousin. Pia chooses whether to use it. Jody saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The million-dollar flat*, Jody says, “I built the first kitchen cabinets here. I'd like to recover them before a rich buyer throws them away.”
connections: Remy Cruz. A dependable custody handover and a year of treatment both earn places on the thank-you wall.

reactions.situation: A colleague leaves a name off the thank-you wall
reactions.response: Pia allows a private thank-you to stay private even on unveiling day.
